q: Lawvere's fixed point theorem (the abstract diagonalization principle) implies which of the following results as special cases?
opts: Cantor's theorem (no surjection A→Aᴬ), Gödel's incompleteness, Rice's theorem, and Curry's paradox
The spectral theorem for compact operators
exp: Lawvere's theorem: in any Cartesian closed category, if there is a surjection A→Aᴬ, every endomorphism of A has a fixed point. Contrapositive: if some f: A→A has no fixed point, no surjection A→Aᴬ exists. This unifies: Cantor (|A|<|Aᴬ|), Gödel (self-reference), Rice (undecidability), Curry (inconsistency).
